gen_risks.description: Armed conflict, security instability, and population displacement in FCV areas (such as CAR, Chad, and Cameroon) may disrupt health service delivery and delay project activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct Security Risk Assessments (SRAs), implement Security Management Plans (SMPs), and adopt flexible implementation arrangements tailored to fragile settings.
gen_risks.evidence: Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence, leading to large population displacements.

gen_risks.description: Decentralized implementation across multiple line ministries and field-level activities creates risks of non-compliant or questionable expenditures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update financial management manuals, customize accounting software across PIUs, mandate internal audit work plans, and recruit independent external auditors within six months of effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: several activities under the project like workshops, trainings and the local-level capacity building are at risk to generate questionable expenditures in Cameroon.

gen_risks.description: Weak contract management capacity and restricted market competition in FCV environments could cause procurement bottlenecks and delivery delays for critical health commodities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified procurement specialists, conduct early market engagement for high-value contracts, utilize STEP real-time tracking, and apply flexible procurement methods.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings.

gen_risks.description: Expanded diagnostic and laboratory operations will generate hazardous chemical, biological, and medical waste, posing environmental and community health risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update and implement Healthcare and Biomedical Waste Management Plans (BMWMP), integrate safe storage and disposal standards, and enforce biosafety guidelines across lab networks.
gen_risks.evidence: laboratories will be supplied with reagents, chemicals, and equipment that may constitute medical waste once used.

gen_risks.description: Increased deployment of community health workforces and civil works labor influx heighten risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare country-specific SEA/SH Action Plans, recruit dedicated GBV specialists, establish GBV-sensitive grievance redress mechanisms, and enforce worker codes of conduct.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial... lack of national protocols for the identification and care of survivors of SEA/SH

gen_risks.description: Recurrent climate events such as floods and extreme heat threaten health facility infrastructure and increase vector- and waterborne disease outbreaks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate green and climate-resilient designs (e.g., EDGE certification, solar power) into health facility rehabilitations and integrate early warning climate-health surveillance systems.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change is a primary driver of health emergencies in Central Africa and already has negative impacts on health systems...

gen_risks.description: Vulnerable or disadvantaged groups (such as IDPs, refugees, rural women, and indigenous communities) may face structural barriers to accessing project interventions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement adapted Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEPs), establish accessible local Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRMs), and target inclusive community outreach.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential social risks are substantial and relate to: (i) inadequate stakeholder engagement... (ii) the exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups

gen_risks.description: Complex regional coordination across five implementing entities (CEMAC and four national governments) with differing priorities may cause operational friction and delay regional activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Operationalize the Regional Coordination Committee (RCC) facilitated by CEMAC/WAHO, establish formal MoUs, and utilize standardized regional platforms and protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Effective coordination among CEMAC, national governments, and beneficiaries is essential for successful implementation.

gen_risks.description: Digitization of surveillance and cross-border data sharing could expose sensitive health data to privacy breaches without robust data governance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish standardized data-sharing protocols with strict personal data protection rules in accordance with national laws and international ethics guidelines.
gen_risks.evidence: inadequate attention to ensure that guidelines established under the Program include considerations for and ethical data security protocols

gen_risks.description: Construction or rehabilitation of laboratories, health posts, and emergency centers may lead to land acquisition or localized land use restrictions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Screen project sites during preparation and prepare site-specific Resettlement Plans (RPs) and Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) prior to civil works.
gen_risks.evidence: land acquisition impacts associated with new constructions

gen_risks.description: Fiscal constraints and low domestic health spending in participating countries threaten the long-term financial sustainability of health security infrastructure post-project.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to integrate health security into national Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks, track budget allocations, and explore public-private partnerships.
gen_risks.evidence: low government funding (driven by weak revenue generation and low prioritization of health in the government’s budget) has led to a high reliance on household’s out-of-pocket payments...

gen_risks.description: Gaps in laboratory diagnostic capacity, biosafety standards, and fragile supply chains could hinder timely pathogen identification and early warning response.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish integrated sample transport networks, deploy Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), enforce biosafety standards, and conduct SLIPTA quality audits.
gen_risks.evidence: the region commonly faces significant gaps in laboratory diagnostic capabilities, disease surveillance and information systems, supply chain infrastructure and management...

gen_risks.description: Delays in recruiting key PIU staff (such as FM officers, auditors, and E&S specialists) and establishing steering committees within legal covenant deadlines could slip project timelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize Project Preparation Advances to initiate early recruitment and fulfill dated legal covenants for staffing and software customization.
gen_risks.evidence: CEMAC - Financing Agreement (Schedule 2, Section I.A.1b): The Recipient shall, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, appoint, assign, or recruit...

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
